entries.definition: the planned subjects and learning content of a course
entries.example: The curriculum connects practical tasks with reading and discussion.

entries.definition: a process used to judge learning or performance
entries.example: The assessment checks how learners use the ideas in context.

entries.definition: to judge quality or value using evidence and criteria
entries.example: Students evaluate the two designs against the same requirements.

entries.definition: standards used to judge or decide something
entries.example: The criteria include accuracy, clarity, and respect for the audience.

entries.definition: to gain knowledge or a skill through learning or experience
entries.example: Learners acquire useful expressions by meeting them in varied contexts.

entries.definition: to continue to keep information in memory
entries.example: Regular recall practice can help me retain new vocabulary.

entries.definition: understanding the meaning of something read or heard
entries.example: The questions test comprehension rather than the ability to copy sentences.

entries.definition: the ability to read and write effectively
entries.example: The center offers adult literacy classes in the evening.

entries.definition: a structure of ideas used to organize work or understanding
entries.example: The framework helps teachers connect activities with learning aims.

entries.definition: to combine parts so they work together
entries.example: The course will integrate speaking practice with short reading tasks.

entries.definition: to make a process or activity easier
entries.example: Clear roles can facilitate discussion in a large group.

entries.definition: an experienced person who guides someone less experienced
entries.example: A mentor helped the new teacher reflect on her lessons.

entries.definition: an officially recognized award showing completed education or training
entries.example: The advertisement explains which qualification applicants must hold.

entries.definition: something required before another activity can begin
entries.example: Basic computer knowledge is a prerequisite for the advanced workshop.

entries.definition: financial support given to help someone study
entries.example: The scholarship covers part of her course fees.

entries.definition: money charged for education at a school or college
entries.example: The college publishes tuition costs before applications open.

entries.definition: the act or number of people formally joining a course
entries.example: Enrollment increased after the evening classes became available.

entries.definition: required by a rule rather than freely chosen
entries.example: The safety session is compulsory for every laboratory student.

entries.definition: a course chosen rather than required
entries.example: She selected a photography elective alongside her main subjects.

entries.definition: people working together to create or achieve something
entries.example: The project encouraged collaboration across several subject areas.

entries.definition: the reasons or desire that encourage action
entries.example: Choosing meaningful reading gave him more motivation to study.

entries.definition: the ability to follow a chosen plan despite difficulty
entries.example: A flexible routine can support discipline without demanding perfection.

entries.definition: a natural capacity to learn a particular kind of skill
entries.example: The course values effort as well as aptitude for languages.

entries.definition: a developed level of skill in an activity
entries.example: A single quiz does not establish overall language proficiency.

entries.definition: to add explanatory notes to a text or image
entries.example: Students annotate the article before discussing its argument.

entries.definition: to change writing in order to improve it
entries.example: I revise the opening after receiving comments from two readers.

entries.definition: to combine information from several sources into a new whole
entries.example: The final task asks us to synthesize ideas from three articles.

entries.definition: to think carefully about an experience or idea
entries.example: We reflect on what helped before planning the next study session.

entries.definition: guided by the learner’s own choices and goals
entries.example: Self-directed study still benefits from clear aims and honest feedback.

entries.definition: someone with a similar role or level of experience
entries.example: A peer read my draft from a learner’s perspective.

entries.definition: a guide describing standards for judging a task
entries.example: The rubric explains what a clear explanation should include.

entries.definition: a separate unit within a larger course
entries.example: Each module ends with a short practical activity.

entries.definition: an outline of topics and requirements for a course
entries.example: The syllabus lists the readings and assessment dates.

entries.definition: a lesson that guides someone through a particular subject or task
entries.example: The tutorial demonstrates how to compare two sources.

entries.definition: a selected collection showing someone’s work and development
entries.example: Her portfolio includes early drafts as well as finished essays.

entries.definition: relating to formal study and education
entries.example: The workshop introduces academic writing without unnecessary technical language.

entries.definition: connected with practical training for a particular occupation
entries.example: The vocational program includes supervised practice in a real workshop.

entries.definition: designed so people with different needs can use or understand it
entries.example: The accessible lesson provides clear text and an audio alternative.

entries.definition: allowing people from different groups to take part fairly
entries.example: An inclusive discussion gives quieter participants time to respond.

entries.definition: active interest and involvement in an activity
entries.example: Student engagement improved when the questions related to daily life.

entries.definition: the continued ability to remember learned information
entries.example: The follow-up activity checks retention after a week.

entries.definition: the use of learning in a different situation
entries.example: The role-play encouraged transfer from classroom phrases to everyday requests.

entries.definition: to provide temporary structured help while a skill develops
entries.example: Teachers scaffold a difficult task with examples and guiding questions.

entries.definition: intended to guide improvement while learning is happening
entries.example: The formative quiz shows which topics need another explanation.

entries.definition: used to judge learning at the end of a period
entries.example: The summative task brings together the skills practiced throughout the course.

entries.definition: based on stated evidence or rules rather than personal preference
entries.example: The objective questions use stored answer keys for consistent grading.

entries.definition: influenced by a person’s feelings or judgment
entries.example: A personal reflection may receive subjective comments about style.

entries.definition: intended to help improve something
entries.example: Constructive feedback points to a practical next step.

entries.definition: careful and thorough in checking details and reasoning
entries.example: The project needs rigorous checking before its conclusions are shared.

entries.definition: the ability to make and manage your own decisions
entries.example: Learner autonomy includes choosing goals and checking progress honestly.
